title: I: Jupyter (Python) figures
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests the panzoom extension with the Jupyter engine: the same cell options as the R pages, on matplotlib figures. knitr and Jupyter hand figures to Quarto differently (knitr writes the image markdown itself; Jupyter cells come back as notebook outputs), so the filter has to find the figures and their cell options either way. The document has no lightbox: key, and only marked cells should open the viewer.
Rendering it needs Python with matplotlib and ipykernel: see tests/README.md.
Jupyter leaves the panzoom and lightbox options out of the code shown on the page (knitr shows them); the Code button at the top shows the full source.
Headings carry what the browser test checks, as on the other pages: expect-open, expect-hint, expect-max-zoom and expect-fit.

#| fig-cap: A sine wave.

title: I: Jupyter (Python) figures
text:
6. Wide collage (8 × 0.8 in)
A strip, so it opens at screen height. Jupyter figures are shown at their size in inches × 96 px (Quarto writes it on the image), not shrunk to the column as knitr’s are: a 25 × 2 in collage would be 2,400 px wide on the page, cut off at the column’s edge. This one fits.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: An 8 × 0.8 inch collage of 8 panels.

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 8, figsize=(8, 0.8), layout="constrained")
for ax in axes:
    walk(ax)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=4)
plt.show()
```




An 8 × 0.8 inch collage of 8 panels.

title: G: captions and descriptions
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests citations and cross-references in the viewer. A caption is copied from the page, so whatever Quarto renders there comes through. A description is rendered with the page too, in a hidden block the viewer copies, so its citations resolve, its cross-references get numbers, and a work cited only in a description is still listed under References. Quarto’s own lightbox shows a citation in a caption as raw [@key] (quarto-cli#10709).
Cases 1–5 have the expect-references attribute: the viewer must show at least one citation or cross-reference, none unresolved, and each must link to something on this page. Cases 6 and 7 test the per-cell caption and description options (expect-caption).

title: E: image formats
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests the panzoom extension with the knitr graphics devices used in practice: webp, svg and pdf output, for a wide collage and a standard plot. Every figure is marked with #| panzoom: true and should open the pan/zoom viewer, except where a case says otherwise. Figure shapes and how they open are on H: wide and tall figures.
Headings carry what the browser test checks: expect-fit (the opening view: contain, height or width), shift-scroll (which way Shift+scroll moves the image: x, y or none) and expect-scale="1" (opens at real size, not enlarged).
webp comes from ragg’s agg_webp device: knitr has no built-in webp device, and agg_webp needs units = "in" because knitr passes sizes in inches.

title: E: image formats
text:
1. Wide collage, webp (25 × 2 in)

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 96)
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 panels (webp)."

collage()
```




A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 panels (webp).

title: E: image formats
text:
6. png + cairo_pdf (dev: [png, cairo_pdf])
Like case 5, with the cairo PDF device, which embeds fonts and handles Unicode (µ, Greek letters) and transparency better than pdf. The page shows the png either way. With a PDF device alone, there is no image to open: Quarto embeds the PDF in a small box with the browser’s PDF viewer, which panzoom leaves alone.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: !expr c("png", "cairo_pdf")
#| fig-cap: "png shown, cairo_pdf written alongside (mu = 5, alpha = 0.05)."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors,
               plot.title = title(main = "mu = 5, alpha = 0.05"))
```




png shown, cairo_pdf written alongside (mu = 5, alpha = 0.05).

title: E: image formats
section: 7. Wide collage, webp at 2× resolution (100 × 5 in)
text:
7. Wide collage, webp at 2× resolution (100 × 5 in)
At 192 dpi the collage is 19,200 px wide, beyond webp’s limit of 16,383 px per side; this case records what happens.

```{r}

#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 192)
#| fig-cap: "The collage as webp at 192 dpi."
#| error: true

collage()
```




The collage as webp at 192 dpi.

title: panzoom
text: This is a Quarto extension that opens figures in a full-screen viewer, built on Panzoom: scroll to zoom toward the cursor, drag to pan, double-click or 0 to reset, Esc to close. It attempts to match, and extend, the feature set of Quarto’s built-in lightbox. Source and documentation: https://github.com/sekoclancy/panzoom.

title: panzoom
text:
Chunk output
Mark a code cell with #| panzoom: true. Click the figure to open it, scroll to zoom toward the cursor, drag to pan, double-click to reset, Esc to close.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4

image(volcano, col = hcl.colors(100, "Viridis"), asp = 1 / 3)
```

title: panzoom
text:
Cross-referenced figure
Labeled figures work too (Figure 1). Options under #| panzoom: override the document’s settings for one cell: this figure zooms to 10 instead of the page’s 6, and hides the hint.

```{r}
#| label: fig-volcano
#| fig-cap: "Maunga Whau volcano."
#| panzoom:
#|   max-zoom: 10
#|   hint: false

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```







Figure 1: Maunga Whau volcano.

title: panzoom
text:
Markdown image



A markdown image with the .panzoom class.

title: panzoom
text:
Captions and galleries
The viewer shows the figure’s caption. Plots with the same group form a gallery: use the ‹ › buttons, ←/→ or a swipe to step through them. Subfigures of one figure are a gallery automatically.
```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: volcano-views
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Volcano heights as an image."
#|   - "The same data as a perspective plot."
#| layout-ncol: 2

image(volcano, col = hcl.colors(100, "Viridis"))
persp(volcano, theta = 135, phi = 30, col = "green3", shade = 0.5, border = NA)
```






Volcano heights as an image.







The same data as a perspective plot.





```{r}
#| label: fig-volcano-sub
#| fig-cap: "Two views of Maunga Whau, as subfigures."
#| fig-subcap: ["Contours", "Filled contours"]
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| panzoom: true

contour(volcano)
image(volcano)
```











(a) Contours











(b) Filled contours







Figure 2: Two views of Maunga Whau, as subfigures.

title: panzoom
panzoom
text:
Test pages
The same 12 lightbox situations (galleries, subfigures, captions with math, images in links, margin images, …) rendered four ways:

A: Quarto lightbox reference: Quarto’s built-in lightbox alone.
B: marked images + lightbox: the usual setup, lightbox: true with some images marked for panzoom.
C: panzoom match: auto: panzoom picks the images itself.
D: explicit marking: images marked with .panzoom or #| classes: panzoom.

And pages of their own:

E: image formats: webp, svg and pdf output.
F: options: opting out, and the hint, max-zoom and loop options.
G: captions and descriptions: citations and cross-references, and the caption and description options.
H: wide and tall figures: 25 × 2 inch collages, tall strips, galleries and layouts of them, and the fit option.

title: B: panzoom on marked images, Quarto’s lightbox on for the rest
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests the usual setup: Quarto’s lightbox is on for the document (lightbox: true), and only some images are marked for panzoom, with .panzoom or #| classes: panzoom. The markup is the same as in d-panzoom-selective, which has no lightbox.
The marked images should open the pan/zoom viewer; every other image should open Quarto’s lightbox, as in a-lightbox. Case 6’s first chunk has both classes: panzoom and #| lightbox: options on purpose: panzoom should win, so it doesn’t join GLightbox’s gallery. Case 8 (#| lightbox: false) gets neither. Case 9’s link should still work (images inside links are left alone).

title: F: options
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests panzoom’s options one at a time: opting out with .nopanzoom and #| panzoom: false, and the per-cell hint and max-zoom options. The page itself sets loop: true, so the gallery in case 6 wraps around. There is no lightbox, so an image panzoom leaves alone opens nothing. The caption and description options are on G: captions and descriptions, fit on H: wide and tall figures.
Each case says what to expect in its heading’s attributes (expect-open, expect-hint, expect-max-zoom), or on a single image, and the browser test checks them.

title: H: wide and tall figures
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests how the viewer opens figures of different shapes: very wide collages (25 × 2 inches), tall strips, a poster, a portrait photo and a small plot, alone, in galleries and in layouts, and the fit option. All are png; other formats are on E: image formats.
By default (fit: auto) very wide figures open at screen height from the left end (or where they were clicked), very tall ones at screen width from the top, and everything else whole, never enlarged past its real size.
Headings carry what the browser test checks: expect-fit (contain, height or width), shift-scroll (which way Shift+scroll moves the image: x sideways, y up and down, none, or zoomed-x: sideways after zooming in until the image extends past the screen both ways) and expect-scale="1" (opens at real size), expect-zoom-out (yes: the opening view is closer than the whole image, so it zooms out; no: it already is the whole image). The first single collage and image shown whole also get the focal point and containment checks.

title: H: wide and tall figures
text:
1. Wide collage, png (25 × 2 in)

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 panels (png)."

collage()
```




A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 panels (png).

title: H: wide and tall figures
text:

The override for case 1: the whole collage, as a strip.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: contain
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "The collage, forced to open whole."

collage()
```




The collage, forced to open whole.

title: H: wide and tall figures
text:

Wide, but readable whole: the size rule leaves it alone.

```{r}

#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 4

```




A 4:1 figure.

title: H: wide and tall figures
text:
4. Tall strip (4 × 15 in)

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap: "A tall strip of 8 panels."

set.seed(2)
par(mfrow = c(8, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:8) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
```




A tall strip of 8 panels.

title: H: wide and tall figures
text:
5. Large poster (24 × 18 in)
Opens whole; zoomed in, it extends past the screen both ways, and Shift+scroll moves sideways.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 18
#| fig-cap: "A 24 × 18 inch poster of 48 panels."

set.seed(3)
par(mfrow = c(6, 8), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:48) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
```




A 24 × 18 inch poster of 48 panels.

section: 8. fit: height on an ordinary plot
text:
8. fit: height on an ordinary plot
On a screen wider than the plot (1.4:1), filling the height is already the whole plot, so this opens like fit: contain and can’t zoom out. Case 15 shows fit: height on a figure where it differs.

```{r}

#|   fit: height

wave(3)
```

#| panzoom:

Second collage.

title: H: wide and tall figures
text:
11. Gallery of two tall strips
Each strip opens at screen width and extends downwards: Left/Right do nothing (there is nowhere to go sideways) rather than switch strips; the ‹ › buttons switch.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: strips
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First strip."
#|   - "Second strip."

for (k in 1:2) {
  set.seed(10 + k)
  par(mfrow = c(8, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in 1:8) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Strip", k, "row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
}
```




First strip.







Second strip.

title: H: wide and tall figures
section: 15. fit: height on a wide figure (12 × 4.5 in)
text:
15. fit: height on a wide figure (12 × 4.5 in)
Not a strip (shown whole it is over a quarter of the screen tall), so fit: auto would open it whole. fit: height opens it filling the screen height (but not past its real size), from where it was clicked, and zooms out to the whole figure.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: height
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5

collage(6)
```

title: H: wide and tall figures
section: 16. Case 15 with a long caption and description
text:
16. Case 15 with a long caption and description
The caption and description sit below the image; fit: height fills the height left above them, so it opens smaller than case 15. The caption scrolls past a quarter of the screen, the description past a fifth, so the image keeps at least about half.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: height
#|   description: "A long description, to take room below the image. Each panel is a random walk of 200 steps, drawn with base R's `plot()` in a one-row layout (`par(mfrow = c(1, 6))`), coloured along the `hcl.colors()` palette. The figure is 12 by 4.5 inches, which knitr writes at 192 dpi (2304 by 864 px). With `fit: height` the viewer opens it as tall as the space above this text allows, and no taller than its real size. Drag or use the arrow keys to move along the figure, scroll or press - to zoom out to the whole of it, and 0 to come back to this opening view."
#| fig-cap: "Six random walks side by side, opened with `fit: height` under a long description."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5

collage(6)
```




Six random walks side by side, opened with fit: height under a long description.





A long description, to take room below the image. Each panel is a random walk of 200 steps, drawn with base R’s plot() in a one-row layout (par(mfrow = c(1, 6))), coloured along the hcl.colors() palette. The figure is 12 by 4.5 inches, which knitr writes at 192 dpi (2304 by 864 px). With fit: height the viewer opens it as tall as the space above this text allows, and no taller than its real size. Drag or use the arrow keys to move along the figure, scroll or press - to zoom out to the whole of it, and 0 to come back to this opening view.
